hints.title: Locate the centre first
hints.body: Complete the square separately in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> terms and in the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> terms of the circle equation.
hints.recap: In <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>, the centre is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.
hints.pitfall: The signs of the centre coordinates are opposite to the signs inside the brackets.
hints.pause: Write down the centre in terms of the given constants.

recall.reminder: Use completed squares to read a circle centre.

hints.title: Express the requested distance
hints.body: Use the coordinate differences between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow></math> and the centre to write <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>. You need the centre-to-point distance, so decide which features of the circle enter that expression.
hints.recap: The squared distance between two points is the sum of the squares of their coordinate differences.
hints.pitfall: Knowing a circle radius alone does not locate an arbitrary point relative to its centre.
hints.pause: Identify which listed collection of constants determines your whole expression, and why the other collections leave something undetermined.

recall.reminder: Distance calculations can be handled through squared coordinate differences.

solution:
Completing squares gives (x+f)2+(y+g)2=f2+g2−h, so the centre is (−f,−g). Hence L2=(p+f)2+(q+g)2.

Knowing f,g,p,q determines L. The constant h controls the radius and is not needed for this distance. Option A does not locate P; C leaves the centre coordinate −g unknown; D leaves −f unknown.

Answer: B.
knowledgePattern: Separate centre data from radius data in a distance calculation
